chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: If a man enters upon a woman while she is pregnant and assaults her, causing what is in her womb to be killed, and then she attacks him and kills him—he said: “The blood of the thief is wasted without compensation, and the blood-money for her child is upon the ʿāqilah.”

key_terms.الْمَعْقِلَةِ: the ʿāqilah, the legally responsible kin-group bearing the diya
key_terms.بَطْنِهَا: her womb or belly, referring here to the unborn child in pregnancy
key_terms.دِيَةُ وَلَدِهَا: the blood-money due for her unborn child
key_terms.ذَهَبَ دَمُ اللِّصِّ هَدَرًا: the assailant’s blood is without compensation
key_terms.فَقَتَلَ: he killed; here, caused death through the assault

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pregnant woman kills an assailant who caused the death of her unborn child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a violent assault against a pregnant woman. It states that the aggressor's blood is without compensation when she kills him in response, while liability for the unborn child’s diya is assigned to the ʿāqilah.
